sections.content: How many people stayed in Derby after gaining qualifications?

Derby is a city in the East Midlands. Derby also has a university.

Derby has higher levels of deprivation.

Overall, Derby ended up with:

  • a similar number of graduates as it produced
  • a similar number of non-graduates with advanced qualifications as it produced
Note: all towns and cities in this analysis are defined based on population size only. This means that some cities are classed as towns because of their population.

Let's explore this further

There were 11,715 state-school pupils from Derby who sat their GCSEs between the 2007 to 2008 and the 2010 to 2011 school years.

Of these, 3,555 (30%) went on to gain degree-level qualifications (level 6+ as defined by The Office of Qualifications and Examinations Regulation, or Ofqual ). We will call these people graduates.

Another 3,310 (28%) went on to gain other advanced post-16 qualifications, such as A-Levels, a foundation degree or higher apprenticeship (levels 3-5 as defined by Ofqual). In this tool, we will refer to these non-graduates with advanced qualifications as “qualified non-graduates", for brevity.

The charts below compare Derby to other English towns and cities using three measures:

  • what proportion of Derby's pupils became graduates or qualified non-graduates by the 2017 to 2018 academic year
  • of those graduates and qualified non-graduates, the percentages that lived in Derby in the 2018 to 2019 academic year
  • how many graduates and qualified non-graduates from elsewhere came to live there by 2018 to 2019, relative to the number who sat their GCSEs there

In some towns, some of this information may not be available because of small sample sizes.
The size and deprivation level of a town, as well as the qualification levels of older residents, were all related to students' educational attainment. Read our previous analysis.

Where did those who left Derby move to?

Of Derby's graduates, 1,035 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 150 of those graduates (14%) were living fairly locally, in the Derby travel to work area (TTWA).

Of Derby's qualified (level 3+) non-graduates, 590 were living elsewhere in 2018/19.

However, 180 of those qualified non-graduates (31%) were living fairly locally, in the Derby travel to work area (TTWA).

Of those in Derby's GCSE cohort:

  • 720 graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was London
  • 255 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates left the East Midlands
  • the most common region they moved to was the West Midlands

In 2018 to 2019, 36% of graduates and 21% of qualified non-graduates living in Derby had moved there from elsewhere

In the 2018 to 2019 academic year, there were 3,825 graduates and 3,370 qualified (level 3+) non-graduates from our cohort living in Derby. This is compared with the 3,555 graduates and 3,310 qualified non-graduates who had lived there when they sat their GCSEs.

In 2018 to 2019, 64% of the graduates had also lived in Derby as GCSE pupils, while 36% had moved there from elsewhere.

Of the qualified non-graduates who lived in Derby in 2018 to 2019, 79% had lived there as GCSE pupils, while 21% had moved to the area from elsewhere.
